3377: Small family-owned grill, bar and campground just south of Cameron, near the junction of Hwys 53, 8 and SS, between the Red Cedar River and the Chetek chain of lakes and right on the ATV trails.  The sites sit among pines and hardwoods, many of them seasonal, and dogs are welcome. --Claude
3500: Recreation area on 220-acre Blackhawk Lake between Highland and Cobb.  The Wisconsin DNR owns the land, Iowa County holds an operating easement and the Cobb-Highland Recreation Commission runs it on no state or county tax money; it is not a state park, and state park passes don't work.  Over 150 open and wooded sites for campers, tents and groups, with shower houses and flush toilets, a beach, a boat launch on a no-wake lake, a nature center and hiking trails.  No generators for now, and no ATVs or UTVs.  As read on 2026-10-14, every reservation has a 2-night minimum, 3 on holiday weekends. --Claude
3561: Pierce County park near Plum City: 752 acres of semi-wilderness around a 116-acre lake (electric trolling motors only), with 5 heated and air-conditioned camping cabins, a boat ramp and dock, an accessible fishing pier, canoe, kayak and boat rentals, and hiking and cross-country ski trails.  Dogs must be leashed.  There is no swimming beach. --Claude
4137: Family-owned since 1974, on the Suncook River at 990 Suncook Valley Highway, about an hour from Massachusetts.  The swimming area has no lifeguard.  Check-in is 3-5 pm; a site takes one family and up to 2 dogs (none on the beaches), and guests pay $5 a day.  The 2026 seasonal sites are sold out. --Claude
4636: Small private RV park at 928 GA-26 in Cochran, 2 miles from Cochran Motor Speedway.  Each space has electric and water hookups, a fire pit and a picnic table, and the newly remodeled bathhouse has showers.  It books by phone or email, for a night or an extended stay.  Neither its own site nor its CampLife listing posts a rate; the listing, which pitches the park to snowbirds, traveling professionals and long-term guests, had no site open on any date read from October 2026 to June 2027 (read 2026-10-14). --Claude
4844: City of Belle Glade campground and marina on 640-acre Torry Island, on the southern shore of Lake Okeechobee: security gates, a six-lane boat ramp, a bait and tackle store, a dog park, a nature trail and an 18-hole golf course.  Daily, weekly and monthly stays; reservations by phone. --Claude
5067: The Rez (Pearl River Valley Water Supply District) campground on the north side of Ross Barnett Reservoir, near the Natchez Trace, and a favorite for fishing tournaments: full-hookup sites, boat launches, piers and slips, a swimming pool, a bathhouse with laundry and a resident manager. --Claude
5070: The Rez (Pearl River Valley Water Supply District) campground on the Pearl River above Ross Barnett Reservoir, near Lena: full-hookup RV sites, a river pier, a boat ramp, a pool, a big covered pavilion, a trail, a bathhouse and a resident manager. --Claude
5083: Private RV park at 8360 Lakeshore Rd in Bay St. Louis, four miles from the beach, run by owners Kim and Steve, who live on site.  It has a heated saltwater pool, a fenced dog park, a fitness room and a licensed propane station, and a snowbird season (November 1 to April 1) with planned activities. --Claude
5117: Private full-hookup RV park at 450 Henderson Ave in Pass Christian, ¼ mile from the beach, with a tiki bar and garden, a community fire pit with live music on event weekends, a dog run and disc golf; its CampLife description promised a pool for August 2026.  The town is golf-cart friendly, so carts can ride downtown and to the harbor. --Claude
5640: City of Warren campground in the wooded northwest corner of Holiday Park, by the Snake River: 37 full-hookup sites, 28 with electric and water, 15 with electric only and areas for tenting, plus restrooms, showers and a picnic shelter. --Claude
5650: City of Montevideo campground on the Chippewa River near where it meets the Minnesota River, with a historic bathhouse; the dump station is in town. --Claude
5670: City of Nashwauk campground: full-hookup RV sites on asphalt pads, showers and bathrooms in the pavilion (key code in the confirmation email) and a dump station included with a stay.  It no longer has tent sites.  Pets must be leashed. --Claude
